items.title: Blizzard Reveals the World of Warcraft Forever Feature 'We Simply Must Hold the Line On'
items.description: Ever since Blizzard revealed World of Warcraft: Forever at Blizzcon 2026, the company has been laser-focused on maintaining its Classic+ identity, even if that means not implementing some quality-of-life features the game's retail version has had for years.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Ever since Blizzard revealed World of Warcraft: Forever at Blizzcon 2026, the company has been laser-focused on maintaining its Classic+ identity, even if that means not implementing some quality-of-life features the game's retail version has had for years.

In a reply to GingiTV and Nobbel87, two of the biggest WoW personalities on X/Twitter (albeit from complete opposite ends of the community), Blizzard developer Josh Greenfield confirmed that not implementing shared drops and tagging was "one of those things that we simply must hold the line on." He continued, saying "It’s hard to see the value in something like this when you are frustrated in the moment but it is extremely important to our social pillar to maintain some of this friction."

Yep, this. This is one of those things that we simply must hold the line on. I think there are other things we can do to help alleviate some frustration here but shared tagging is not it.

It’s hard to see the value in something like this when you are frustrated in the moment but…

— Josh Greenfield (@AggrendWoW) September 20, 2026

In the retail version of World of Warcraft, players who are questing or trying to farm rare spawns can all tag the same enemy (to a limit), so that everyone can get the rewards for killing it. This makes it a lot easier to play the game outside of a group, but it all but eliminates the need to group up with other players outside of high-end group content like dungeons and raids.

It's not hard to see why some people would want shared tagging implemented in Forever, too. The beta for this new version of old World of Warcraft has been incredibly popular, which means there's a lot of competition for anyone that just wants to kill some boars for some bones. The solution, which was suggested by Nobbel and confirmed by Greenfield is to "group up and get it done together," which will give people more opportunity to socialize, which is really what WoW Forever is designed for.

To Blizzard's credit, it seems like a huge portion of WoW Forever players agree with its approach. Most of the replies and quotes of Greenfield's post are along the lines of "The Classic team we trust 💙" from MrGMYT, and "shared tagging taught players to pay less attention to each other and soon became less social" from covingtown.

World of Warcraft: Forever is currently in Beta, which you can access by spending $60 on the Skyborne pack, but you'll only be able to play until level 20. The full game will launch on November 4, and will be included in your World of Warcraft subscription, just like any other version of Classic.

items.title: Sega Planned to Kill Sonic the Hedgehog Before Movie Success
items.description: Sega bosses were ready to ditch Sonic the Hedgehog before the franchise's hugely-successful live-action movie helped change their minds.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Sega bosses were ready to ditch Sonic the Hedgehog before the franchise's hugely-successful live-action movie helped change their minds.

That's according to Sonic Team leader and development veteran Takashi Iizuka, who has worked as a designer, director and producer on more than 30 games featuring Sega's mascot over the past three decades.

While the idea of Sega ditching Sonic seems shocking — akin to Pokémon abandoning Pikachu, or Mario shaving off his moustache — the Sonic series has certainly faced some tough years. Indeed, as Iizuka has now admitted, his tenure in charge of the blue blur included "good times" and also "the worst times."

"It has been 35 years, which means it has been longer than actually my children, so I look upon this franchise like sort of like my own son," Iizuka told One More Game. "There had been good times, and there had been bad times... during the worst times, I was told by the higher-ups that we should cancel the entire franchise.

"I had to fight within the organization to keep the franchise as long as possible," Iizuka continued. "The biggest milestone for me was the first movie, that had been a great hit and definitely changed the course of this franchise."

Released in 2020, the first Sonic movie ended up earning a surprisingly solid $320 million and kickstarting a successful blockbuster franchise — though its success was far from assured. The series almost failed before it ever got started after the movie's first trailer was widely mocked for its "ugly" Sonic design, including horrible teeth. In a now-legendary move, Sega then decided to delay the movie to completely revise Sonic's design, ensuring it more closely matched the hedgehog's in-game appearance — and the rest is history.

Now, Sega has plans to continue pushing Sonic further beyond games, even if the hedgehog's foundation will remain on PC and consoles. Next year will see the launch of a fourth Sonic movie, a Netflix animation series is on the way, and Iizuka has said he expects "some sort of media almost every year from here on out."

"The franchise itself is rooted in video games," Iizuka concluded, confirming that Sega had no plans to ditch Sonic anymore. "We're just going to base everything upon the video games. That's our core principle."

What's next for Sega's Sonic game series? Iizuka says he has identified a desire from fans for more "more emphasis on story. So in coming years, I really want to create some game that has more emphasis on story." Iizuka also said he'd like to include more Shadow the Hedgehog, a character that he and an increasingly vocal group of fans both seem to enjoy. "If you have played Sonic Adventure 2, people may know that Shadow basically sort of died at the end of that game," Iizuka noted. "We were originally intending to just kind of 'die the character out' [kill him off'], but the character Shadow was just so very popular that we decided to revive him in Sonic Heroes."

In the meantime, Sonic the Hedgehog 4 launches in theaters on March 19, and the character is currently involved in a major crossover with Fortnite.

media:description.$text:
Sonic the Hedgehog 4

The Sonic movies are going strong (Sonic 3 is at the top of our best video game movies of all time list!), so it's no surprise that a fourth film is in the works. There aren't many details available about the project yet, but based on the Sonic 3 post-credits scene, expect Amy Rose and Metal Sonic to show up.

Release Date: March 19, 2027

items.title: Adidas Officially Launches Limited-Edition Pokémon Collection
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Adidas just dropped its limited-edition Pokémon collection, the latest in a pretty wild list of collaborations celebrating the franchise’s 30th anniversary.

The full collection includes over 10 new designs for a mix of the company’s most popular sneaker styles, including the Samba and Superstar II. Each shoe has an entirely distinct look inspired by a specific Pokémon, and the stars of the show aren’t too surprising.

Prices range from $60 to $180 with full family sizing. Even better? Every sneaker is available to buy right now.

Adidas Just Dropped Its 30th Anniversary Pokémon Collection

  • See the collection at Sole Play
  • See the collection at Adidas
  • See the collection at Foot Locker

Some features, like the gold embroidered Pokémon x Adidas logo, appear across the collection, but each shoe generally stands on its own two feet (get it) as a unique release. Here’s the full list of what’s available in specific styles:

Every New Sneaker in the Adidas x Pokémon Collection

  • Pikachu - Superstar II (Yellow) and Superstar II (White)
  • Gastly - Adistar Control 3 (Out of Stock)
  • Haunter - Adistar Control 5
  • Gengar - Adistar XLG 2.0 (Out of Stock)
  • Charmander - Superstar II
  • Charmeleon - Superstar II
  • Charizard - Superstar Vintage
  • Rayquaza - Adistar Control 5
  • Mewtwo - Samba

As you can tell, the collection includes a mix of full evolution lines (i.e. Charmander to Charizard) as well as some particularly iconic individual Pokémon like Pikachu and Mewtwo.

I got the chance to check out three specific shoes from the collection of time, and let’s just say I’m impressed. I don’t typically go for the most colorful looks in the world, but the designs have a range of boldness that lets you pick a vibe that goes best with your style. And, of course, based on whichever Pokémon you like best.

The Mewtwo Superstars are a soft purple with a sleek iridescent sheen. While every shoe includes a token-esque shoelace charm with its featured Pokémon’s face, this pair also comes with a funky “liquid” tag featuring the legendary’s classic Psystrike move. On the bolder side, the Charmander sneakers show a full graphic of the Pokémon blowing some literal Ember into the iconic Samba stripes.

It’s cool to see each shoe get its own little deep cut reference to a Pokémon’s type and even specific moveset. The (new!) illustrations of each Pokemon are all high quality, and the shoes themselves are, as you’d expect, pretty darn comfy.

As a limited-edition collection, it’s worth noting that stock may be limited. The Pokémon TCG side of things has been plagued by an ongoing scalping crisis that, these days, seems to extend to anything connected to the Nintendo franchise.

Speaking of, the collection forms part of some pretty extensive celebrations for Pokémon’s 30th anniversary. The beloved media powerhouse currently stands as the highest-grossing franchise of all time, and has already launched unique anniversary collaborations with Puma, Crocs, and even Krispy Kreme. I’m sure we’ll see plenty of more announcements through the end of the year, which, at the very least, will bring us slightly closer to the next mainline Pokemon generation.

items.title: Microsoft Signals Intention to Close Down Ninja Theory After Deals to Save the Hellblade Developer Fall Through
items.description: Microsoft has signalled its intention to close down Hellblade developer Ninja Theory after two deals to save the Xbox studio fell through.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Microsoft has signalled its intention to close down Hellblade developer Ninja Theory after two deals to save the Xbox studio fell through.

In-line with UK employment law, a consultation with the staff at the Cambridge-based studio has begun. While Microsoft has said it is now working to close the studio, it remains open to an agreement to rescue the company.

"Unfortunately, two separate agreements for Ninja Theory fell through," Xbox Chief Content Officer Matt Booty said in a blog post issued today. "We will now begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward."

In June, at an Xbox Games Showcase event, Microsoft announced Senua, the third game in the Hellblade series. At the time, there was little concern about the game’s release. Indeed, there was little concern, publicly at least, about Ninja Theory itself.

But that all changed when optimism sparked by the positive showcase was shattered by new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” memo, which suggested mass layoffs and studio closures were to come. Confirmation came in July, when Ninja Theory was among the studios on the Xbox chopping block.

Amid the reports, fans expressed confusion at how Microsoft could announce Senua from Ninja Theory and then just days later tell the studio’s staff it planned to shut the company down. According to Game File, Microsoft allegedly planned to close or spin off Ninja Theory when it revealed Senua, and it did so thinking that “the promise of a newly announced game would help draw investor interest in the studio.”

Clearly, that plan has failed.

Will Senua ever come out? IGN has yet to comment, but it’s looking increasingly unlikely unless a dramatic, 11th-hour deal can be struck that would save not just the studio, but the Hellblade franchise. Perhaps giving Ninja Theory hope is that Psychonauts developer Double Fine and South of Midnight developer Compulsion both navigated their way to independence and brought their intellectual property along with them, as well as funding for new games. Microsoft, it seems, is willing to part with IP to help get its studios out the door.

Ninja Theory’s Hellblade games have struggled commercially, and Microsoft is currently doubling down on its big franchises in a bid to raise revenue and profitability. It’s focusing on the likes of Minecraft, Halo (which is now under Activision’s umbrella), Fallout, and The Elder Scrolls as it looks to turn around the Xbox business over the next few years.

For more on all the big changes at Xbox announced today, check out our roundup.

items.title: CONFIRMED: Microsoft Hands Halo to Call of Duty Developer Activision as Part of Seismic Xbox Studios Shakeup
items.description: Microsoft has today confirmed that the next mainline Halo game will be developed by Call of Duty maker Activision, with mass layoffs hitting Halo Studios amid a significant restructure of its Xbox studios setup.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Microsoft has today confirmed that the next mainline Halo game will be developed by Call of Duty maker Activision, with mass layoffs hitting Halo Studios amid a significant restructure of its Xbox studios setup.

Xbox announced 268 layoffs today "across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer" as part of the ongoing cuts first announced in July. The layoffs, the majority of which are at Halo Studios, come as part of new Xbox boss Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft's gaming business that had already seen 1,600 staff lose their jobs in the summer. At the time, Microsoft said another 1,600 staff on top would also go this financial year.

"The actions completed since July, inclusive of the studio divestitures, bring us roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring," Xbox Chief Content Officer Matt Booty said in a blog post. "I am deeply grateful for what our colleagues have built, and I know how difficult today will be for those leaving and the teams around them."

With Halo Studios gutted, Microsoft has handed Halo to Activision. Activision will develop "the next Halo title," Booty said, "led by a new, purpose-built team that is separate from ongoing development and plans for Call of Duty. A small team at Halo Studios will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market."

Booty did not say when the next Halo game will come out, or if Activision plans to reboot the series or rotate it into its schedule of releases for Call of Duty, which hasn’t missed an annual release for 20 years.

Halo moving to Activision follows a string of tough releases for the franchise under Xbox's stewardship. Microsoft bought the Halo franchise when it purchased its original developer, Bungie, in 2000. Bungie then split from Microsoft to become independent again in 2007, and went to work on looter shooter Destiny as part of a high-profile, 10-year publishing deal with Activision. Meanwhile, Microsoft set up 343 Industries, so named after 343 Guilty Spark from the Halo games, to take Halo into a new era. 2012's Halo 4 was the first Halo game released by 343. It was followed by 2015's Halo 5: Guardians, which in turn was followed by 2021's much-delayed Halo Infinite. Halo Infinite in particular struggled, and this year's Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the beloved first Halo game, suffered problems of its own.

In 2024, 343 Industries changed its name to Halo Studios and announced plans to work on multiple new Halo games that would all be developed on Epic's Unreal Engine. The announcements were unveiled in a seven-minute video shown ahead of the Halo World Championship's grand finals, which showcased the results of Project Foundry — an experimental project designed to show a Halo game built using Unreal Engine. While it was not much more than a tech demo, the video offered a glimpse at a fresh beginning for Xbox's flagship franchise in the wake of Halo Infinite's troubled launch. The question is, will any of that work be carried forward by Activision? Check out Ryan McCaffrey's reaction to today's Xbox news in his opinion article, Can Activision Save Halo?

Meanwhile, Xbox has moved Age of Empires developer World's Edge and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under the Activision umbrella, without confirming the legendary British studio's next game.

Rob Kostich, president of Activision issued the following statement:

"We’re thrilled to welcome Halo, Rare, and World’s Edge to Activision. It’s an honor and a responsibility that we do not take lightly. These teams and their games have inspired fans around the world for decades.

"For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place. It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.

"To the World’s Edge and Rare teams, we can’t wait to get to work together."

Outside Activision, Obsidian, developer of Grounded, The Outer Worlds, and Avowed, is now a Bethesda studio, as it begins work on a new Fallout game. Forza Motorsport developer Turn 10 is being merged with Forza Horizon and Fable developer Playground, and Candy Crush developer King now includes Microsoft Casual Games, which operates the likes of Solitaire, Mahjong, and Minesweeper.

Microsoft has also signalled its intention to close Hellblade developer Ninja Theory after two separate deals for a sale fell through. As per UK employment law, a consultation with staff has begun. Ninja Theory was working on the third entry in the Hellblade series, called Senua, but that game's future is in doubt.

There is no further news on the fate of Blade developer Arkane. Microsoft is currently negotiating with management over the future of the studio, following French employment law, so the process is further behind that of other Xbox studios. Booty said "consultation with Arkane remains underway and is expected to continue through the end of the year."

Psychonauts developer Double Fine and South of Midnight studio Compulsion had already managed to navigate their way to independence as part of the Xbox reset. Today, Booty confirmed that Undead Labs has now "successfully transitioned" on "similar terms" and, with a new publisher, will release State of Decay 3 day one on Game Pass.

"The goal is to strengthen our franchises and games by operating fewer business units, aligning groups that already work closely together, and focusing our publishing expertise," Booty added.

Today’s dramatic news sparks a number of unanswered questions: what does the future of Halo look like? What does Activision plan to do with Rare and Sea of Thieves? And where will the rest of the layoffs Microsoft announced were in the works in July come from?

The Xbox reset is the most significant restructure in the history of Microsoft's gaming business, and forms part of Sharma's drive to reach a billion people each day through video games by 2030. It follows continued poor financial results for Xbox and a collapsing profit margin, which Sharma has set about turning around by cutting costs and doubling down on big franchises such as Halo, Minecraft, and Fallout.

"Today, our focus should be on supporting those affected and treating one another with care and respect," Booty added. "I will spend time with our studios over the next week. At our October 6 town hall, we will come together as an ALL-XBOX team to reflect on our progress and look ahead to one of the strongest game lineups in our history."

It was followed by 2015's Halo 5: Guardians, which in turn was followed by 2021's much-delayed Halo Infinite. Halo Infinite in particular struggled, and this year's Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the beloved first Halo game, suffered problems of its own.

In 2024, 343 Industries changed its name to Halo Studios and announced plans to work on multiple new Halo games that would all be developed on Epic's Unreal Engine. The announcements were unveiled in a seven-minute video shown ahead of the Halo World Championship's grand finals, which showcased the results of Project Foundry — an experimental project designed to show a Halo game built using Unreal Engine. While it was not much more than a tech demo, the video offered a glimpse at a fresh beginning for Xbox's flagship franchise in the wake of Halo Infinite's troubled launch. The question is, will any of that work be carried forward by Activision? Check out Ryan McCaffrey's reaction to today's Xbox news in his opinion article, Can Activision Save Halo?

Meanwhile, Xbox has moved Age of Empires developer World's Edge and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under the Activision umbrella, without confirming the legendary British studio's next game.

Rob Kostich, president of Activision issued the following statement:

"We’re thrilled to welcome Halo, Rare, and World’s Edge to Activision. It’s an honor and a responsibility that we do not take lightly. These teams and their games have inspired fans around the world for decades.

"For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place. It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.

"To the World’s Edge and Rare teams, we can’t wait to get to work together."

Outside Activision, Obsidian, developer of Grounded, The Outer Worlds, and Avowed, is now a Bethesda studio, as it begins work on a new Fallout game. Forza Motorsport developer Turn 10 is being merged with Forza Horizon and Fable developer Playground, and Candy Crush developer King now includes Microsoft Casual Games, which operates the likes of Solitaire, Mahjong, and Minesweeper.

Microsoft has also signalled its intention to close Hellblade developer Ninja Theory after two separate deals for a sale fell through. As per UK employment law, a consultation with staff has begun. Ninja Theory was working on the third entry in the Hellblade series, called Senua, but that game's future is in doubt.

There is no further news on the fate of Blade developer Arkane. Microsoft is currently negotiating with management over the future of the studio, following French employment law, so the process is further behind that of other Xbox studios. Booty said "consultation with Arkane remains underway and is expected to continue through the end of the year."

Psychonauts developer Double Fine and South of Midnight studio Compulsion had already managed to navigate their way to independence as part of the Xbox reset. Today, Booty confirmed that Undead Labs has now "successfully transitioned" on "similar terms" and, with a new publisher, will release State of Decay 3 day one on Game Pass.

"The goal is to strengthen our franchises and games by operating fewer business units, aligning groups that already work closely together, and focusing our publishing expertise," Booty added.

Today’s dramatic news sparks a number of unanswered questions: what does the future of Halo look like? What does Activision plan to do with Rare and Sea of Thieves? And where will the rest of the layoffs Microsoft announced were in the works in July come from?

The Xbox reset is the most significant restructure in the history of Microsoft's gaming business, and forms part of Sharma's drive to reach a billion people each day through video games by 2030. It follows continued poor financial results for Xbox and a collapsing profit margin, which Sharma has set about turning around by cutting costs and doubling down on big franchises such as Halo, Minecraft, and Fallout.

"Today, our focus should be on supporting those affected and treating one another with care and respect," Booty added. "I will spend time with our studios over the next week. At our October 6 town hall, we will come together as an ALL-XBOX team to reflect on our progress and look ahead to one of the strongest game lineups in our history."

items.title: DCU Chief James Gunn Hits Back at Lanterns Criticism Over 'Killing' Hal Jordan 'Right Away'
items.description: DC Universe co-CEO James Gunn has hit back at criticism of HBO show Lanterns for apparently killing Hal Jordan “right away.”
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
DC Universe co-CEO James Gunn has hit back at criticism of HBO show Lanterns for apparently killing Hal Jordan “right away.”

The first episode of Lanterns showed a murdered Hal Jordan, played by Kyle Chandler, in 2026 before going back in time to 2016 to tell a seemingly unrelated story.

Warning! Spoilers for Lanterns follow…

Showing the much-loved Hal Jordan with a hole in his head in the first episode of the show sparked a significant backlash from fans who had waited years for his live-action depiction in the DCU. Episode 6 doubled down on this by showing Hal’s funeral.

But there are question marks hanging over Hal’s death. Indeed, some aren’t convinced he’s dead at all. Following the conclusion of Episode 5, Lanterns has moved back to 2026 and switched into “whodunnit?” mode, with the central storyline revolving around John Stewart’s bid to solve the mystery of Hal’s murder. Some fans believe that over the course of the final two episodes, it will be revealed that the real Hal Jordan is alive and kicking, and the frozen corpse we saw in Episode 1 was a copy of some kind. (We recently explored the many ways Lanterns could explain that Hal is still alive.)

Still, some fans are very upset at Hal’s apparent death, and are sending angry messages to James Gunn on social media about it. Gunn actually responded to one person who had this to say:

“Maybe you should try and at least respect the characters that made the comics popular. Killing Hal off right away after we have waited 15 years to see him on screen again was the worst thing you could have done.”

Gunn clearly didn’t like that, and in his response dropped a clue that fans who think Hal is alive are on the right track.

“Hal's the star of TV series & he's in all the episodes so far,” Gunn began. “It's more live action screen time than all the live action screen time he's had combined throughout history. Kyle is amazing in the role. We more than respect him. We love him, despite his imperfections. Us knowing the time of his death, if that's exactly what that is, is absolutely not the same thing as killing him off right away. Hal is a big reason why the show is so popular with fans & non fans alike; sorry if you don't like it.”

Gunn’s position on this is clear: he feels like Hal’s had plenty of time on-screen over the course of the show, and it’s true he’s played a starring role in all the episodes so far. But it’s the line about his death that is being highlighted by fans:

“Us knowing the time of his death, if that's exactly what that is, is absolutely not the same thing as killing him off right away.”

“... if that’s exactly what that is,” is a line that, for some fans, pretty much confirms that there’s more to Hal’s death than it seems. Certainly, Chandler’s portrayal of Hal Jordan has gone down well with fans, who would love to see the character continue in the ongoing DCU. While there’s no suggestion he’s in next year’s Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow, perhaps Gunn could see Chandler reprise the role in some other project, or maybe even a Lanterns Season 2.

Nathan Fillion’s Guy Gardner, however, is proving to be a throughline for the DCU. He’s in Superman, Peacemaker Season 2, Lanterns, and is expected in Man of Tomorrow.

items.title: 'Risky and Gutsy': Resident Evil Movie Star Austin Abrams Reveals His First Reaction to The Film's 'Shocking' Finale
items.description: Resident Evil movie star Austin Abrams has recalled his initial reaction to the film's finale, which he believes is "crazy and shocking."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Resident Evil movie star Austin Abrams has recalled his initial reaction to the film's finale, which he believes is "crazy and shocking."

Warning: spoilers for Resident Evil follow...

Zach Cregger's enjoyable Resident Evil film follows Abrams' everyman courier Bryan as he transports a bag of medical supplies into a deadly zombie apocalypse. Unfortunately, as you'll know from watching the film, Bryan ends up not making it out of Raccoon City alive.

It's a particularly sad ending for Bryan as he's never able to reconnect with his pregnant girlfriend, or make amends with her after an earlier argument. Despite fighting off waves of undead and recording a message of reconciliation for her, Bryan succumbs to his injuries and turns into a monster, just as a cure is produced.

Cregger's ending is certainly a bold choice, and one that differs from the heroic end featured in every Resident Evil game. But Abrams himself is clearly a fan of this story's finale, and described the ending as a "risky and gutsy" decision by Cregger, in an era where downbeat endings are now rarer to avoid bumming out audiences and killing a movie's chance for word-of-mouth recommendations.

"I've been living with it for a while now, but I thought it was crazy and shocking when I first read it," Abrams told The Hollywood Reporter. "I love that Zach takes those risks. You follow this one guy the whole time, so hopefully you’re enjoying watching him and rooting for him. Then to have him not make it is really risky and gutsy, which is what I love about all of Zach’s work. So I was surprised by it, but I also loved that he would take that chance.

"With a lot of movies nowadays, they’re a little too afraid to do something like that — to kill off a character you really like," he concluded. "And if they do, the blow is softened in some way so it doesn't hurt too much. Whereas a lot of older films don’t do that; they just rip your heart out. We're here to feel, man. We're here to go through something. So I'm just appreciative that Zach is willing to take a risk like that."

With all of that said, however, we learned this week that Cregger still tweaked the film's ending in post production using material he'd already shot — if anything to make things even more tragic. There's details here of how things would have originally planned out.

items.title: 'I'm Too Old': Marvel Star Says He's Officially Retired From His Beloved Guardians of the Galaxy Role as Rocket Raccoon
items.description: Marvel actor Sean Gunn has officially retired from his role playing Guardians of the Galaxy and Avengers hero Rocket Raccoon.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Marvel actor Sean Gunn has officially retired from his role playing Guardians of the Galaxy and Avengers hero Rocket Raccoon.

After five films and one holiday TV special, Gunn has said he's now "too old" to provide the performance capture for the beloved Rocket (whose voice is then dubbed in post-production by Bradley Cooper).

Speaking to podcast host Brandon Davis, the Gilmore Girls legend said he had made the decision to depart his role as Rocket after recently turning 50, and noticing that the amount of crouching he'd had to perform for the part was beginning to have an effect on his "physiology."

On set, behind the scenes footage has featured Gunn scuttling around the legs of his Marvel co-stars while squatting down in what he describes as a "catcher's crouch" position. Thankfully, Gunn could also stretch his legs and stand up to also play Kraglin, the Ravager who ultimately ends the sci-fi saga as a fully paid-up Guardians member.

"Everyone thinks it's my knees but it's really my feet and my ankles," Gunn said, describing the physical difficulty he has faced after portraying Rocket Raccoon. "Because I'm in a catcher's crouch and I'm pivoting a lot on my points of contact with the ground... I'm doing a lot of pivoting in my ankles and feet. And over the years I think it had a little bit of an effect on my physiology.

"My knees are fine but since I turned 50 a couple of years ago I am retired from Rocket," he admitted. "Not that they've called but if they did, I don't think I could do the motion reference for Rocket anymore. I'm too old."

When might we see Rocket again? It's hard to say. Marvel is yet to confirm its future plans for the Guardians of the Galaxy, which remains a hugely popular team of characters, though one whose story has reached a natural conclusion. Gamora is off with the Ravagers, Drax and Nebula are looking after an array of children, while Mantis has also gone off to find her own path.

Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 ends with a new team forming, featuring Rocket, Groot, and Kraglin joined by Adam Warlock, Cosmo the Space Dog, and Phyla. It's unclear if any of the above characters will ever return to the MCU, and it seems unlikely we'll get another Guardians of the Galaxy movie any time soon, with its writer and director James Gunn (yes, Sean Gunn's brother) now heading up the DCU. But Marvel has promised that Chris Pratt's Star-Lord will appear at some point (our best guess would be in Avengers: Secret Wars).

But even if Rocket Raccoon is invited back for the Multiverse Saga's big finale, it'll be someone else who squatted down to portray him instead.

Image credit: Eric McCandless/Disney via Getty Images.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda Movie Actress Posts Cryptic Tease, Raising Hopes for an Imminent Trailer
items.description: The Legend of Zelda movie star Bo Bragason has raised hopes of an imminent trailer release for Nintendo's upcoming film.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The Legend of Zelda movie star Bo Bragason has raised hopes of an imminent trailer release for Nintendo's upcoming film.

With just seven months to go until The Legend of Zelda arrives in theatres, Nintendo and Sony (which is distributing the film) are yet to show anything of it in motion. Sure, we've had a few photos of Bragason in costume as Zelda, alongside House of the Dragon actor Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Link. But there has been no sign of a teaser, and still no official confirmation of the film's wider cast — despite many unofficial reports now having emerged.

Could all of that change today? Fans certainly believe so, as Bragason posted on Instagram last night to say she was "excited 4 tomorrow." Bragason regularly posts on Instagram about her upcoming projects, though has acknowledged she can say nothing specific at all about The Legend of Zelda, which Nintendo is keeping under lock and key.

Fans had hoped we'd see something more of the film in this month's recent Zelda-focused Nintendo Direct, but in reality there was little to add. Nintendo confirmed that The Legend of Zelda would be the movie's name, and acknowledged it would be an original story inspired by the franchise so far, rather than a direct adaptation of any particular game.

Originally announced in 2023, The Legend of Zelda is helmed by Maze Runner and Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes director Wes Ball, while Nintendo's legendary Shigeru Miyamoto is listed as a co-producer, alongside Marvel production veteran Avi Arad. The movie was shot last winter in New Zealand, with the Middle-earth-like location now doubling for Hyrule.

Unofficially, it's been reported that Dichen Lachman (Severance) will play Impa, while Uli Latukefu (Black Adam) will play Ganondorf. These will be joined by other castmates such as Yvonne Strahovski, Lydia Peckham and the late Sam Neill. While their roles have yet to be disclosed, Deadline reported that the former will be playing a "queen" character.

Could we see them confirmed officially today? Time will tell. But what we do know for sure is that The Legend of Zelda is currently set to arrive in theaters on April 30, 2027.

Image credit: Jason Mendez/Getty Images for Prime Video.

items.title: Here's Your First Look at 3 Cards From Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign, Due to Launch This November
items.description: IGN can today reveal three new Pokémon card designs from the upcoming set Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
IGN can today reveal three new Pokémon card designs from the upcoming set Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign.

Due to launch on November 6, this latest batch of Mega Evolution-themed cards includes creatures such as Mega Malamar, Mega Golurk and Mega Rayquaza, with over 135 designs in total.

Today, we can show off our first look at starter Sprigatito, the Grass Cat Pokémon, as well as both of its evolutions, Floragato and Meowscarada.

Sprigatito's design shows the cute kitty settling down for a late morning nap on a trainer's bed. Its 70 HP is decent, though its Play Rough attack lacks a little punch.

It's lucky, then, that you can evolve Sprigatito into Floragato, with 90 HP and the Slash attack for a chunkier 60 damage. With that on the board, you're on your way to playing Meowscarada ex, which lands with a solid 320 HP and the strong Magical Bullet attack, that can deal a whopping 120 damage to its opponent, and another 120 damage to any damaged benched Pokémon. As with all ex cards, though, Meowscarada will count for two prizes if knocked out.

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution — Delta Reign will be the next set to launch following the current Pokémon 30th Anniversary release, which arrived last week to huge demand, queues, fights, and ultimately some disappointment from scalpers who haven't been able to turn their usual profits. Oh dear!

items.title: Injustice 3 Leak Reportedly Reveals 2 Playable Characters
items.description: Injustice 3 will feature one character fans will expect and one who perhaps comes as a surprise, according to a fresh leak.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Injustice 3 will feature one character fans will expect and one who perhaps comes as a surprise, according to a fresh leak.

MP1st unearthed evidence to suggest the unannounced fighting game will feature both Supergirl and Batwoman on its roster of playable characters. Supergirl comes as no surprise, given her starring role in the nine-year-old Injustice 2. But Batwoman’s inclusion — assuming it’s true — would mark the debut for the character in the mainline Injustice games.

Batwoman (Kate Kane) dies in the canon Injustice comics, which suggests someone else has taken up the Batwoman mantle for Injustice 3, Kate Kane didn’t actually die, or the game retcons the events of the book. Either way, this is a superhero story we’re talking about — no-one stays dead forever.

Or, as MP1st suggests, Injustice 3 may not continue the story told in Injustice and Injustice 2, but act as a reboot that tells an entirely different story. NetherRealm’s other fighting game franchise, Mortal Kombat, has done this multiple times, so it wouldn’t be a huge surprise with Injustice since it’s been nearly a decade since Injustice 2 came out.

Publisher Warner Bros. has yet to announce another Injustice game, despite it being an open secret at this point. Given Paramount looks like it’s finally going to get the green light to complete its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros., perhaps that will provide some clarity on the company’s video game plan, which we know also include Hogwarts Legacy 2 and a new Batman game from Arkham developer Rocksteady.

My guess is Injustice 3 — or whatever it’s called — is announced at The Game Awards in December, with a release set for in or around April 2027.

In May, NetherRealm development chief Ed Boon said another Mortal Kombat game was in development, which again, didn't come as much of a surprise. Confirmation of another Mortal Kombat game came after 2023’s Mortal Kombat 1 sold 8 million copies, just over half Mortal Kombat 11’s total of 15 million copies sold, as of 2022. Perhaps this new Mortal Kombat game will be released after Injustice 3.

The first game in the series, Injustice: Gods Among Us, launched in 2013, with its sequel, Injustice 2, coming out in 2017. NetherRealm released Mortal Kombat 11 in 2019 and for a time it seemed like the studio would alternate between Mortal Kombat and Injustice games, but it went on to release another Mortal Kombat, the soft reboot that is Mortal Kombat 1, in 2023 instead.

Batwoman (Kate Kane) dies in the canon Injustice comics, which suggests someone else has taken up the Batwoman mantle for Injustice 3, Kate Kane didn’t actually die, or the game retcons the events of the book. Either way, this is a superhero story we’re talking about — no-one stays dead forever.

Or, as MP1st suggests, Injustice 3 may not continue the story told in Injustice and Injustice 2, but act as a reboot that tells an entirely different story. NetherRealm’s other fighting game franchise, Mortal Kombat, has done this multiple times, so it wouldn’t be a huge surprise with Injustice since it’s been nearly a decade since Injustice 2 came out.

Publisher Warner Bros. has yet to announce another Injustice game, despite it being an open secret at this point. Given Paramount looks like it’s finally going to get the green light to complete its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros., perhaps that will provide some clarity on the company’s video game plan, which we know also include Hogwarts Legacy 2 and a new Batman game from Arkham developer Rocksteady.

My guess is Injustice 3 — or whatever it’s called — is announced at The Game Awards in December, with a release set for in or around April 2027.

In May, NetherRealm development chief Ed Boon said another Mortal Kombat game was in development, which again, didn't come as much of a surprise. Confirmation of another Mortal Kombat game came after 2023’s Mortal Kombat 1 sold 8 million copies, just over half Mortal Kombat 11’s total of 15 million copies sold, as of 2022. Perhaps this new Mortal Kombat game will be released after Injustice 3.

The first game in the series, Injustice: Gods Among Us, launched in 2013, with its sequel, Injustice 2, coming out in 2017. NetherRealm released Mortal Kombat 11 in 2019 and for a time it seemed like the studio would alternate between Mortal Kombat and Injustice games, but it went on to release another Mortal Kombat, the soft reboot that is Mortal Kombat 1, in 2023 instead.

items.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Update to Add Easier Difficulty Setting for Players Who Don't Want Combat
items.description: The first major The Blood of Dawnwalker update will introduce an easier difficulty option for "people who don't want to experience combat" when it launches in October.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
The first major The Blood of Dawnwalker update will introduce an easier difficulty option for "people who don't want to experience combat" when it launches in October.

Developer Rebel Wolves' game director, Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, teased the changes coming to the team's breakout vampire RPG during a new interview with Eurogamer. Amongst a batch of combat tweaks and other gameplay changes, one of the highlights for the early October The Blood of Dawnwalker update includes reworked difficulty options for players who don't want to spill too much blood during the story.

When the update launches, players will see the new easier difficulty option replace the current easiest mode, called Story Mode, and adopt its name. The version of the mode currently in the game will seemingly be bumped up a peg and given a new name. The Blood of Dawnwalker currently has four difficulty modes – Story, Fair, Challenging, and Duelist – with next month's addition set to bring the total to five.

"We will introduce an additional difficulty level, but an easier one, because many people are asking for a more easy difficulty," Tomaszkiewicz said. "The Story mode which we have right now will be a different difficulty — we will call it Demanding or something like this — and we will add a new Story mode which will be even easier for people who don't want to experience the combat, they just want to learn the story and go through the game without this gameplay challenge."

How exactly The Blood of Dawnwalker will tackle an easier difficulty mode is unclear. The game director's comment suggests it will cater to those who want to skip combat altogether, though how this will be achieved is unclear. There's no release date for the update just yet, but with its launch set for early October, we won't have to wait too long.

Rebel Wolves is also looking into improving gameplay performance, especially for PC users, as well as a fluid option for players to escape fights if they bite off more than they can chew. Other items on the docket include targeting and the camera. Tomaszkiewicz referenced desires from players to tweak how targeting works for Coen and how the upcoming patch will address that.

"There will be three hits you need to take off this stun," he said. "We will see how people will react to that because, as I said, it can create another bad feel, but we will see. Maybe people will switch between targets fluently and if they want to just stun, it will be fine, and if they want to stun and hit a few times, it will be also fine. We will see."

Everything else set to come to The Blood of Dawnwalker in the October patch has yet to be revealed. Although other features, including new game plus, are confirmed to be in the cards, the team is still charging ahead following its successful launch.

It was released for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S September 3 and reached more than 1 million copies sold in just two days. For more on The Blood of Dawnwalker, you can read about how Bandai Namco and Rebel Wolves managed to bring their vision to life on a $40 million budget. You can also learn about how some players are using a mod to bypass one of the game's core mechanics.

items.title: Love Nikki Player Shuts Down Fan Website Over Game's 'Irreverent' and 'Demonic' Clothing Designs
items.description: A fan of the Love Nikki – Dress Up Queen mobile dress-up game is going viral for shutting down their informative website after determining that some of the game’s clothing designs were “demonic.”
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
A fan of the Love Nikki – Dress Up Queen mobile dress-up game is going viral for shutting down their informative website after determining that some of the game’s clothing designs were “demonic.”

Nikki’s Info was a fan-made website compiling many of Love Nikki’s clothes, accessories, story guides, update details, and other information. An X/Twitter account for the site was created in 2018, and players could subscribe to the administrator’s Patreon for exclusive game guides and other insights.

Those players are now being offered refunds after the site’s admin announced that they are quitting the game due to their religious beliefs, as described in a now-viral blog post.

The admin published the post after a week of inactivity on the Nikki’s Info website, which has been completely wiped of any information relating to the dress-up game. They explained their absence in the post, saying they had “done some horrible things involving the occult” and that the “devil had then gained such a foothold in my life [that] I was firmly in his grasp.”

“All of this started quite small and personal — but quickly escalated, where in the end I was in a situation where I was in a near-death situation involving police, paramedics, and other people, of whose kindness I am grateful for. I [was] on the precipice of a terrible situation — [I] called out to God for help. He answered. I then continued to practice the occult. Things got worse again and started affecting others, especially my suffering family, in a way I can’t declare publicly,” they wrote.

While the poster confirmed that they are now fine, they expressed some issues with the clothing designs in Love Nikki, finding them to be blasphemous with “demonic” undertones.

“The game features a lot of crosses as dress-up items, which are irreverent to God, the God who so kindly and patiently saved me. The God I love,” they continued. “There’s a lot of them, disproportionately so. Some are mixed in with gothic demonic themes. Such things, though they might seem small, carry consequences and meaning. This is not to say that playing the game directly led to what happened to me. I can say with some degree of certainty, it really was the terrible things I did. But in the ‘back story,’ the various games, books, works of fiction, movies, even music — they are there.

“I have wrestled with this, but ultimately I can’t profit from or promote something which offends my God, my Saviour — therefore the site is now closed. The source code, the data, the domain are not for sale.”

⭐Behind the Seams | [Version 2.0 5-Star Outfits] The Inspirations Behind the Designs pic.twitter.com/KMOoKqvo67

— Infinity Nikki (@InfinityNikkiEN) December 10, 2025

The admin’s post has gone viral within the broader Infinity Nikki community, sparking concerns from players and theories as to what clothing items specifically led them to this conclusion.

Some pointed out the oddness of the situation, given that a fair few designs within the Nikki franchise were directly inspired by figures within the Catholic religion. For example, Love Nikki includes an outfit set that’s essentially a Pope-like ensemble, while the official Infinity Nikki X account shared a graphic with specific details about how the team at Infold approached its Behind Prayers outfit set, saying the Starlight Crown headdress incorporated “imagery of the Virgin Mary.”

For now, commenters are doing their best to help the Nikki’s Info admin, though the situation has sparked no end of curiosity and debate within the world of dress-up games.

items.title: Call of Duty YouTuber Launches Petition to Remove Skill-Based Matchmaking Following Successful Destiny Protests
items.description: Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests.

The YouTuber has been an outspoken advocate against Call of Duty's SBMM and has tried to make noise on the issue in a variety of ways. Last week, he began tweeting at Xbox CEO Asha Sharma about the matter every day in hopes of getting her attention. Now, he's trying a different way. After seeing Destiny fans successfully rally together to get Bungie to resurrect the sci-fi MMO, Tdawgsmitty decided to try to bring Call of Duty fans together in hopes of a similar outcome.

The YouTuber launched a petition which has gained over 500 signatures in roughly an hour. The call to action aims to get SBMM entirely removed from Call of Duty's unranked lobbies, citing frustrations with the current system and how Activision uses data analysts to develop its matchmaking. Instead, he wants the series to utilize SBMM in the game's ranked play, where players deliberately choose to have a more competitive experience.

"Former Call of Duty developer Brian Bright recently shared that his team’s work on [the canceled Call of Duty game NX1] focused on ping and region," reads the description for the petition. "He also stated that Activision eventually began hiring data scientists who worked with its marketing department to push for more skill-based matchmaking. His statement raises serious questions about how matchmaking priorities evolved.

"For players like us, today’s public matches too often feel like the same competitive experience on repeat. Experimenting with a different weapon, relaxing after work, or playing with friends of different skill levels can become frustrating. When every lobby feels like another test, the fun starts to disappear."

The YouTuber also asked for clearer communication regarding matchmaking and the opportunity for the community to test changes itself. The petition comes roughly a month ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release, which will utilize a divisive SBMM system that was introduced earlier this summer in Black Ops 7. Some feel that Call of Duty's SBMM is too punishing and can result in matches that feel consistently unfair, leading to years of frustrations about the franchise's multiplayer.

Whether a petition can change the mind of Activision remains to be seen, but it's not entirely out of the question. Bungie opted to return to Destiny 2 after killing it earlier this year. There was extreme backlash to the initial decision and players decided to make their voices heard through online protests, which included players choosing to not support Bungie's latest game, Marathon. The developer announced that it will be restoring vaulted content and plans to keep supporting the Destiny franchise, leading to an enthusiastic response from fans. Tdawgsmitty cited this as proof that change is possible.

"This Destiny news is huge for gaming," he said on Twitter. "It shows we can use our voice and effect change. It's time for the COD community to step up and get some much needed changes to the direction its been headed."

If Call of Duty fans can rally together by signing petitions, making their voices heard online, and vote with their wallet, it may very well lead to changes. However, Call of Duty is a massive franchise, and as a result, it may be difficult to make the same kind of dent. IGN spoke with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's lead multiplayer developers in August and asked about how the studio is approaching SBMM.

"I think it's a conversation that we'll continue to have," said Jacky Reynolds, Multiplayer Design Lead at Infinity Ward. "I don't think it's ever going to be a solved system. There's always going to be new iterations that can be made. I think at the end of the day, yeah, we want players to be able to play and have fun. I think that we want to also make sure that they have variety in their matches. I think it's a conversation that we should continue to have. It's also worth mentioning that Joe and I aren’t directly in charge of matchmaking. We are focused on building cool stuff, but I think we're looking forward to seeing how it all shakes out."

items.title: Bloodborne Movie Reveal Reactions Were '80% Critical,' Jacksepticeye Says
items.description: Bloodborne movie producer and YouTuber Jacksepticeye has teased more details about the upcoming animated adaptation after reactions to his involvement were "80% critical."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Bloodborne movie producer and YouTuber Jacksepticeye has teased more details about the upcoming animated adaptation after reactions to his involvement were "80% critical."

The famed content creator, whose real name is Seán McLoughlin, touched on his attachment to Sony's animated take on FromSoftware's beloved action game during an interview with 100 Questions with Tom Simmons (via GamesRadar). He took the opportunity to not only tease how his Bloodborne won't retell the story of the franchise's one and only proper installment, but also discussed how fans reacted to his role as its producer.

"Bloodborne, obviously, is my favorite game ever, so when I got that call, part of me is like… obviously I was going to do anything, but I wouldn't have let it go in a direction that I don't think is worthy of the Bloodborne IP," Jacksepticeye explained. Then, when asked if he was feeling the pressure to deliver, he said, "Oh yeah."

"I'd say 80% of the responses were critical of it," he said, referring to his involvement in the animated film. "I don't want to say 'negative,' because a lot of people were just… I would be the same if someone took my beloved IP, that's my favorite, and then some YouTuber's attached to it. It would just make you scratch your head a little bit."

Sony unholstered its plans for an animated R-rated Bloodborne movie back at CinemaCon 2026 in April. For some, the reveal was a bit of a double-edged sword, as begging to see more from FromSoftware's Lovecraftian action-horror universe seemed to deliver a project that came out of left field in more ways than one.

Jacksepticeye, a self-proclaimed Bloodborne fanatic, is in the mix as one of its producers. He's joined by PlayStation Productions and Lyrical Animation. Shortly after its reveal, the YouTuber called the opportunity "a dream come true" and "the honor of my life."

He also acknowledged that a lot of Bloodborne fans were probably surprised to hear his name attached to an official project in that universe. Regardless of the shock, it's not a project he wants anyone to be worried about, saying that he "will fight tooth and nail to make this thing the best it possibly can be."

When asked during the new interview about what fans can look forward to when it comes to the animated movie, Jacksepticeye assured watchers that he's "not trying to be the game."

"I'm not trying to one-up the game, and I'm not trying to compete with it, or tell the same story," he explained. "I'm trying to honor the universe that's there and tell as good a story as I can within it."

He continued, saying he has "quite a bit" of sway in the overall production and direction of the Bloodborne movie. During calls about the project, he said that "people listen to me above most anyone else."

"I'm the one being like, 'This is a good idea. This is a bad idea. We shouldn't do this,'" Jacksepticeye elaborated. "But also, I'm the one greenlighting who gets hired and who we work with to make sure that vetting process is good.

"You don't want to bring on anyone that has no idea what Bloodborne is. In simpler terms, I'm sort of the vibe-checker."

The Bloodborne movie currently has no release date. While we wait to learn more about it, you can check out IGN's original 9.1/10 review of the game. You can also read more about Jacksepticeye's approach to the film.

The famed content creator, whose real name is Seán McLoughlin, touched on his attachment to Sony's animated take on FromSoftware's beloved action game during an interview with 100 Questions with Tom Simmons (via GamesRadar). He took the opportunity to not only tease how his Bloodborne won't retell the story of the franchise's one and only proper installment, but also discussed how fans reacted to his role as its producer.

"Bloodborne, obviously, is my favorite game ever, so when I got that call, part of me is like… obviously I was going to do anything, but I wouldn't have let it go in a direction that I don't think is worthy of the Bloodborne IP," Jacksepticeye explained. Then, when asked if he was feeling the pressure to deliver, he said, "Oh yeah."

"I'd say 80% of the responses were critical of it," he said, referring to his involvement in the animated film. "I don't want to say 'negative,' because a lot of people were just… I would be the same if someone took my beloved IP, that's my favorite, and then some YouTuber's attached to it. It would just make you scratch your head a little bit."

Sony unholstered its plans for an animated R-rated Bloodborne movie back at CinemaCon 2026 in April. For some, the reveal was a bit of a double-edged sword, as begging to see more from FromSoftware's Lovecraftian action-horror universe seemed to deliver a project that came out of left field in more ways than one.

Jacksepticeye, a self-proclaimed Bloodborne fanatic, is in the mix as one of its producers. He's joined by PlayStation Productions and Lyrical Animation. Shortly after its reveal, the YouTuber called the opportunity "a dream come true" and "the honor of my life."

He also acknowledged that a lot of Bloodborne fans were probably surprised to hear his name attached to an official project in that universe. Regardless of the shock, it's not a project he wants anyone to be worried about, saying that he "will fight tooth and nail to make this thing the best it possibly can be."

When asked during the new interview about what fans can look forward to when it comes to the animated movie, Jacksepticeye assured watchers that he's "not trying to be the game."

"I'm not trying to one-up the game, and I'm not trying to compete with it, or tell the same story," he explained. "I'm trying to honor the universe that's there and tell as good a story as I can within it."

He continued, saying he has "quite a bit" of sway in the overall production and direction of the Bloodborne movie. During calls about the project, he said that "people listen to me above most anyone else."

"I'm the one being like, 'This is a good idea. This is a bad idea. We shouldn't do this,'" Jacksepticeye elaborated. "But also, I'm the one greenlighting who gets hired and who we work with to make sure that vetting process is good.

"You don't want to bring on anyone that has no idea what Bloodborne is. In simpler terms, I'm sort of the vibe-checker."

The Bloodborne movie currently has no release date. While we wait to learn more about it, you can check out IGN's original 9.1/10 review of the game. You can also read more about Jacksepticeye's approach to the film.

items.title: Pokémon Scalper Reportedly Arrested After Punching Man in the Face Over 30th Anniversary Target Drop
items.description: A Pokémon scalper has reportedly been arrested and trespassed after punching a man in a viral confrontation that resulted in a four-year-old child getting hurt in the chaos.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
A Pokémon scalper has reportedly been arrested and trespassed after punching a man in a viral confrontation that resulted in a four-year-old child getting hurt in the chaos.

A Target store in Lisbon, Connecticut is at the center of a viral incident that occurred on August 28, 2026. Footage from the ordeal spread across social media in late September, showing two scalpers with a cart full of Pokémon merchandise making their way to the shop’s self-checkout stations.

The person who recorded the footage confronted the duo along with his girlfriend, who submitted the footage to PokéStreetz, an account dedicated to exposing bad behavior within the Pokémon TCG community.

In the footage, the four parties argued about the amount of merchandise the scalpers were making off with; the scalpers themselves proudly said, “Damn straight” that they were checking out with all that merch, rather than abiding by the two-per-person limit enacted by Target, and warned the couple not to touch their shopping cart.

The recorder and his girlfriend continued to follow the scalpers up to a self-checkout station, where one of the scalpers decked the recorder in the face, causing him to drop his phone on the ground. Scuffling can be heard in the background, along with a child crying.

PokéStreetz claimed that the recorder fell into this child, a four-year-old girl, after being punched by the scalper. The girl also reportedly fell in the impact and hurt her elbow; although the recorder “immediately” went to check up on the girl, the scalper fled, allegedly leaving his wallet behind.

🚨 TARGET RESTOCK ENDS WITH A PUNCH & A CHILD GETS HURT?! OH NAAAA 🚨

📺 This Morning on PokéStreetz

📍 Target — Lisbon, CT
📅 August 28, 2026 | ⏰ Around noon

The submitter says she & her boyfriend were fourth or fifth in line when two shoppers ahead allegedly filled their… pic.twitter.com/0b7BpAS3WO

— PokéStreetz (@POKESTREETZ) September 5, 2026

According to the account, the scalper was arrested and trespassed from the Target after he returned to retrieve his wallet. PokéStreetz also claimed that the father of the injured girl called police after staff at Target allegedly declined to take action.

The scuffle was verified by a local TCG player in a Pokémon drops and restocks Facebook Group, who described the situation as a “nightmare.”

“Lisbon Target was a nightmare today,” they wrote. “Needless to say, they are changing some things I believe, also no UFC if anyone was looking for that lol. Someone went and whipped out all the Hops and AH tins, then when they got recorded at the front, they got violent and punched someone in the face. I didn’t get names or anything, but it was not the normal crew, as I am somewhat of a hang-around sometimes, and none of the regulars were there.”

No police records or local reports regarding the scalpers’ supposed arrest and trespassing have been located thus far. The incident is one of several that have broken out amid Pokémon's 30th Anniversary celebrations, where special collaborations, merchandise, and trading card drops have resulted in chaos.

For example, the hype around Pokémon's 30th Anniversary September trading card drop went viral for the sheer amount of customers who lined up outside shops hours before launch, with some camping outside, while others ‘reserved’ their spots with ‘ghost chairs’ as crowds of fans vied for the chance at snagging some packs.

Luckily, the powers that be seem to have made enough cards to go around this time, and it’s hurting scalpers; a scalping Discord group made the rounds on social media after moaning that the excessive stock was hurting their businesses.

Image Credit: Kindel Media, The Pokemon Company

items.title: Rockstar Games Is Taking Down Footage and Images of Scrapped GTA 5 DLC And Early Version of Leaked GTA 6 Map
items.description: Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content.

Last week, a ton of files for Grand Theft Auto 5 leaked online. These were reportedly obtained during the 2022 hack, which also resulted in the first-ever footage of GTA 6 leaking online. These files have been rumored for some time, but are only just now surfacing publicly. They include cut dialogue from GTA 5, which also seems to hint at different outcomes for the story, such as a darker ending for Franklin. However, the two biggest things are details of a scrapped Liberty City expansion for GTA 5 and an extremely early version of GTA 6's map.

Given that this material was illegally obtained in a hack and not officially released by Rockstar or datamined through the game's files, the studio's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, is working to scrub the assets from the internet. Various YouTube videos and posts with visuals of the leaked material or clips of the audio have been taken down by Take-Two. It doesn't seem like the company is going scorched-earth like it did for the GTA 6 leaks, but it does appear that content creators who post this material are at risk of copyright strikes.

Take-Two are now taking down YouTube videos regarding the latest #GTA leaks. My video only covered a list of files, a visualisation of the data from one of the files using a fan made tool and one cut piece of GTA V dialogue.

Nothing regarding #GTAVI. The dialogue is probably the… pic.twitter.com/gbaKt2kcX5

— TJGM (@TJGM_) September 21, 2026

We're just two months away from the release of GTA 6, and it's likely that Rockstar's security is going to be at an all-time high. The studio has been compromised by multiple leaks for the last four years, and now it's at a point where the game is likely finished and could be at risk of being spoiled. However, the lack of physical copies will make it a lot harder for things to leak ahead of its release. Given tons of footage managed to surface in August, though, it's not impossible for more things to make their way online.

items.title: Indie Game Developer Accuses Studio of Using AI to Rip Off His Viral Potato Peeling Game
items.description: An indie game developer has accused a fellow dev of using AI to rip off his game, a first-person, physics-based title where players peel potatoes.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
An indie game developer has accused a fellow dev of using AI to rip off his game, a first-person, physics-based title where players peel potatoes.

Independent game developer Rado Klasa is going viral after pointing out a glaring similarity between his game, called 1,000,000 Potatoes, and another title named Potato Please. Both have a similar premise; players peel potatoes using physics-based engines. Each game takes place in a Soviet-style military setting. They both seem horror-adjacent.

Klasa posted about his game back in July; on September 20, game consultant Indie Game Joe shared a trailer for Golden Horn Studios’ Potato Please. It didn’t take long for Klasa to come across the post, prompting him to speak out about what he is calling blatant intellectual theft.

made a dumb little game where you peel 1,000,000 potatoes by hand in a cold soviet warehouse. thought it would take a weekend.

potato 15 had a tooth in it. i kept going.#screenshotsaturday #indiegame pic.twitter.com/WBXx2XRqeI

— Rado Klasa || 🥔WISHLIST 1,000,000 POTATOES 🥔 (@Radoslaw_Klasa) July 25, 2026

Klasa believes that Golden Horn directly stole the idea for his game and accused them of using artificial intelligence to do so, describing the situation as “every indie dev’s worst nightmare.”

“I created this concept for the GMTK game jam,” he explained. “I held off on my Steam page to obsessively polish the mechanics... and it just got cloned and shipped. Probably mostly with a simple AI prompt.”

“I’ve spent time refining the game feel, controls, and details,” he added. “It hurts to see a rushed clone beat me to market, but I refuse to let a cheap copy win. The original version will always have the quality players actually deserve.”

It’s every indie dev's worst nightmare.

I created this concept for the GMTK game jam. I held off on my Steam page to obsessively polish the mechanics... and it just got cloned and shipped. Probably mostly with a simple AI prompt.

Here’s my original build vs theirs 👇 https://t.co/4Ri1y0R3J6

— Rado Klasa || 🥔WISHLIST 1,000,000 POTATOES 🥔 (@Radoslaw_Klasa) September 21, 2026

Curators on Steam are already flagging Potato Please as an “AI imagery Rip off of 1,000,000 Potatoes,” and commenters on social media are offering their support and promising to wishlist Klasa’s game — but Golden Horn is maintaining their innocence.

“We need to address this directly. Calling our game a ‘clone’ and implying it was made with ‘a simple AI prompt’ are serious accusations,” the studio wrote in response to Klasa’s post on X/Twitter. “We had never seen your game before these posts. Potato Please originated independently from a potato meme and video popular in our community.

“Similar concepts are not evidence of copying. Real people have spent significant time designing, modelling, coding and developing this game, and we’re prepared to show our project files and development process if necessary. We’re happy to discuss genuine similarities, but publicly presenting speculation about our team and our work as fact is unfair.”

We need to address this directly. Calling our game a “clone” and implying it was made with “a simple AI prompt” are serious accusations.

We had never seen your game before these posts. Potato Please originated independently from a potato meme and video popular in our community.…

— Potato Please (@potatopleasee) September 21, 2026

Players, however, aren’t convinced of Golden Horn’s story. “Its’ just really f**king weird that somehow you both got Soviet Russia potato peeling sim and your account didn't exist until after the game jam happened,” one user argued.

“This is literally 1:1 the SAME GAME lmao stop lying,” another wrote, while others couldn't seem to uncover the viral meme Golden Horn referenced in its reply.

Still, others have accused Golden Horn of using AI to write their response to Klasa’s post. Potato Please made their account just two months ago, and thus far, have shared no progress videos or screenshots showing them making the game, though this isn’t totally unusual in itself.

For other unique indie games that haven’t been hit with AI allegations, check out our coverage of Stray Dog: nobody cares and Ylem’s Cat, both games where you play as an animal or fight bad guys alongside an animal.

items.title: Daredevil: Born Again Will Reportedly End With Season 3, Showrunner Departs Amidst Post-Production
items.description: Daredevil: Born Again will reportedly end with its upcoming third season.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Daredevil: Born Again will reportedly end with its upcoming third season.

According to The Hollywood Reporter, Daredevil: Born Again will not return for a fourth season. Disney reportedly made the decision following the end of production on the third season, suggesting the show wasn't necessarily designed to end here. Additionally, THR reports that the Marvel series' showrunner, Dario Scardapane, exited the project during post-production. Sources reportedly raised eyebrows at the departure, as it has left the show without a clear leader to finish it. Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 is currently expected to premiere in 2027.

It's unclear if Daredevil: Born Again was canceled or if it truly is just the end of this story. The series wasn't a smash hit when it came to ratings, but was hailed as a success by critics and fans, especially compared to other Marvel shows. Disney has pulled back on Marvel TV series in recent years following a string of mediocre releases, but is still committed to a small handful moving forward. The next Marvel show will be VisionQuest, releasing on October 14. THR also noted that three to five other shows are in development, including a spy series named Zodiac.

Wonder Man was also canceled earlier this summer, despite getting greenlit for a second season. As of right now, it's unclear what Daredevil's future is in the MCU. Fans have wanted to see him in a film, especially after his brief cameo in Spider-Man: No Way Home. As Spidey continues to embrace street-level battles, a Daredevil crossover in the next film could be extremely fruitful.

This is also the second time the Man Without Fear has had his TV time cut short at the third season. Netflix and Marvel pulled the plug on the original Daredevil series in 2018 following a critically-acclaimed third season. A fourth season was expected to follow, but various issues prevented that from happening, such as Disney trying to launch its own streamer with original programming. It took the better part of a decade to get Daredevil back on screen, but fans were excited once it finally happened, particularly because it continued the story of the original show and leveraged its darker tone.

Is this the end of Matt Murdock's journey in the MCU? Only time will tell, but we hope that's not the case.
